# CalendarDatePicker

Header: `winui/ui/datetime/CalendarDatePicker.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/datetime/CalendarDatePicker.hpp`.

A field that shows a date and opens a [CalendarView](calendar-view.md#uicalendarview) under itself to pick one.

The field shows the date in the short date pattern of [regional_date_format()](../core/namespace-ui.md#regional_date_format) (or its own `date_format`), and the placeholder text while no date is picked. A click, Enter, Space, Alt+Down or F4 opens the calendar. Picking a day sets the date and closes it, clicking the picked day again clears the date and keeps it open, and Escape or a click outside closes it without a change. [calendar()](#calendar) is the [CalendarView](calendar-view.md#uicalendarview) in the popup, for its range, first day of the week and blackout dates.

[`ui::CalendarDatePicker`](#uicalendardatepicker) is the declarative form.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::CalendarDatePickerControl picker;
picker.set_header("Arrival");
picker.calendar().set_date_range(ui::today(), std::nullopt); // nothing in the past
picker.on_date_changed([](std::optional<std::chrono::year_month_day> date)
                       { std::printf("%s\n", date ? "picked" : "cleared"); });
```

## `ui::CalendarDatePicker`

The declarative form of [CalendarDatePickerControl](#uicalendardatepickercontrol): a date field with a calendar.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::optional<std::chrono::year_month_day>> arrival;

window.set_content(ui::CalendarDatePicker{
    .header           = "Arrival",
    .placeholder_text = "Pick a date",
    .date             = arrival,
    .min_date         = ui::today(),
});
```

}

### automation_name_fallback

```cpp

```

[automation_name()](../tree/element.md#automation_name)'s fallback when [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name is empty. Default: no inherent name, correct for controls with no visible text of their own ([Slider](slider.md#uislider), [ProgressBar](progress-bar.md#uiprogressbar)), which need an explicit [accessibility()](../tree/element.md#accessibility).name from the caller. A control with its own visible text ([Button](button.md#uibutton), [CheckBox](check-box.md#uicheckbox), [TextControl](text.md#uitextcontrol), ...) overrides this to return it.

### automation_children

```cpp
void automation_children(std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The children an automation client sees under this node, immediate children only. A client walks the tree one level at a time, and the parent comes from [parent()](../tree/element.md#parent). Defaults to every child [for_each_child()](../tree/element.md#for_each_child) lists. Override it only to show a client something else: the children in a different order, or without parts that are only decoration. A composite that is one automation node lists nothing.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A pointer event for this element: the element under the pointer, one inside it that did not handle the event, or the element holding the capture. The position is in layout coordinates ([handle_pointer()](../tree/element.md#handle_pointer)). Return true when the event did something here, and it goes no further up; a handled press also captures the pointer until its release. A control that acts on a press (a click, a toggle, a caret placed, a drag started) returns true for the press and its release, so a list row or a card around it does not act on the same click. Default: false.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

A key for this element: the focused one, or one inside it that did not handle it. Return true when the key did something here, and it goes no further; false lets it bubble on to the parent and then to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Default: false.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

This element's own part of [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick): a clock of its own ([ToolTip](tool-tip.md#uitooltip)'s hover delay, an animation's phase, a caret blink). Runs after the visual layer has advanced and before the children are ticked, which [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick) does by itself. Tick only parts that [for_each_child()](../tree/element.md#for_each_child) does not list here. Default: nothing.
